title: startServer() invoked at module load; no exports, no require.main guard
repro: require('src/index.js') opens a port and connects to the DB. Tests therefore had to spawn a child process and talk HTTP to it, so coverage across the spawn boundary was unmeasurable (~0%).
fix: Split into src/app.js (exports the configured app), src/associations.js (idempotent), src/bootstrap/ensureAdminUser.js, and a thin src/index.js guarded by require.main === module. Verified behaviour-preserving by tests/unit/associations.test.js: 24 models / 64 associations byte-identical before and after.

title: No migration for Sheets/SyncJobs/Settings, and 20260607000000-add-soft-delete depends on Sheets existing
repro: On a fresh database `npx sequelize-cli db:migrate` failed at 20260607000000-add-soft-delete with 'relation "Sheets" does not exist' (it adds attendance.sheetId REFERENCES "Sheets" plus a partial unique index on Sheets). The three tables only ever existed via sync({alter:true}), so a fresh clone could not build a schema at all and 13+ endpoints 500'd.
fix: Added src/migrations/20260606000001-create-sheets-syncjobs-settings.js, dated before add-soft-delete. Settings columns match the raw CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in schedulerService.js:27,270 so that DDL stays a no-op. Verified: all 32 migrations now run green on a fresh DB (25 tables), and re-running on an already-synced DB is a no-op.

title: Test env spread ...process.env and never pinned MAIL_PROVIDER — the suite could send real email
repro: The repo .env sets MAIL_PROVIDER=smtp with live credentials. Any test exercising credential delivery delivered real mail to real addresses; credential-delivery.test.js:54 (asserting provider === 'demo') failed as a side effect.
fix: tests/testEnv.js pins MAIL_PROVIDER=demo and SMS_PROVIDER=demo with no fallback, applied via a setupFiles entry so every project and worker gets it. tests/setupAfterEnv.js throws before any test runs if the pinning has regressed.

title: AUTO_REFRESH_KNOWLEDGE unset in tests — Sequelize hooks fired fetch() at the live chatbot on :8000
repro: Six models debounce a knowledge-refresh POST to CHATBOT_URL on write. Under test this mutated the developer's running chatbot instance and left a dangling timer. The kill switch already existed and was simply unused.
fix: Pinned AUTO_REFRESH_KNOWLEDGE=false and CHATBOT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 (discard port). global.fetch is replaced in setupAfterEnv with a mock that throws, so any unmocked outbound call fails loudly.

title: moment-timezone and moment required by 3 files but undeclared
repro: studentPortalController.js:2, weeklyReportService.js:6 and schedulerService.js:7 require moment-timezone. Both packages were physically present in node_modules but absent from package.json — one `npm ci` from a production crash.
fix: Declared moment@^2.30.1 and moment-timezone@^0.5.48 at their installed versions.

title: readFileSync(keys.json) at module load — keys.json is gitignored, so a fresh clone could not boot
repro: Requiring sheetsService threw before any code ran, taking down every module that transitively imports it.
fix: Deferred to a memoized getSheetsAPI()/getServiceAccountEmail() behind try/catch. The process now starts without credentials and only the Google Sheets endpoints fail, with an explicit message naming the missing path. 9 call sites rewritten.

title: Dead module with a hardcoded /home/addy/... keyFile path
repro: googleSheetsIntegration.js requires 'google-spreadsheets', which is neither declared nor installed, so the module throws on require. Its only consumer, src/middleware/googleAuthMiddleware.js, reads a .auth property the module never exports and is mounted by no router.
fix: Both files deleted. Verified dead first: zero references anywhere in src/ or tests/.

title: Fixture predates 20260722000000-add-section-to-subjects — 32 of 46 cases failed once the schema was complete
repro: POST /api/subjects has required batchId and sectionId since subjectController.js:49-53. The beforeAll sent only subjectCode/subjectName, got 400, and every downstream case failed. Previously masked because the test DB was 4 migrations behind.
fix: Fixture now sends batchId + sectionId (the taught subject in the assigned section, the untaught one in the other section), and asserts 201 on both so a future break surfaces at the right line.

title: Test DB host/port defaulted to localhost:5432 — the wrong Postgres major version
repro: DB_HOST/DB_PORT fell back to Postgres defaults, silently targeting the native :5432 instance instead of the Docker Postgres 15 on :5436 that matches production.
fix: tests/testEnv.js pins 127.0.0.1:5436 with no Postgres-default fallback (overridable only via explicit TEST_DB_HOST/TEST_DB_PORT). setupAfterEnv additionally refuses to run unless DB_NAME is the disposable attendance_db_test.

title: finishAudit is bound to both 'finish' and 'close', writing two audit_logs rows per request
repro: res.on('finish', finishAudit) and res.on('close', finishAudit) both fire for a normal response, so every request inserts the same audit row twice. Separately, the !auditData branch calls next() from inside a response-lifecycle handler — i.e. after the response has already been sent.
recommendation: Guard with a once-flag and drop the next() call from finishAudit. Behaviour-changing (halves audit_logs volume), so it needs your sign-off.

title: IORedis clients constructed at import time — DISABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS cannot prevent Redis connections
repro: Both queue modules `new IORedis(...)` at module scope. Requiring anything that transitively imports them (sheetsController, studentController, syncRoutes, sheetsService, schedulerService) opens a socket to :6379 and keeps the event loop alive indefinitely — `node -e "require('./src/services/sheetsService')"` never exits.
recommendation: Lazily construct the queue behind a getter and return a no-op when DISABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=true. Worked around under test via jest moduleNameMapper to tests/mocks/bullQueue.js; the production defect stands.

title: POST /api/auth/login returns 500 on a request with no email — unauthenticated crash on a public endpoint
repro: curl -X POST /api/auth/login -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' → 500 'WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value'. login() calls validationResult(req) but no validator middleware is attached to the route (authRoutes.js:55), so an empty body flows into User.findOne({where:{email:undefined}}), which Sequelize throws on. Reachable with no credentials, so any unauthenticated caller can force a 500 and a stack trace into the logs.
fix: Explicit guard returning 400 when email or password is absent. Regression covered by 4 cases in tests/int/authz-matrix.test.js ('crash-on-missing-input regressions'), plus a case asserting a wrong password is still 401 rather than 400.

title: GET /api/attendance/search returns 500 when ?email is omitted
repro: GET /api/attendance/search with an ADMIN token and no query string → 500 'WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value'. Same root cause as A-010: an absent parameter reaches Sequelize as where:{email:undefined}. ADMIN-only, so lower severity than A-010.
fix: Guard returning 400 when email is absent; an unknown email still returns 404. Both covered in tests/int/authz-matrix.test.js.

title: authorizeRoles returned an anonymous arrow, making declared authorization invisible to introspection
repro: Walking the live router stack yielded a handler-name histogram of '189 <anonymous>, 5 authenticateJWT, 3 multerMiddleware' across all 169 routes — guards could not be told apart from controllers, so observed behaviour could never be diffed against declared intent.
fix: Name the returned function and attach guard.__allowedRoles = allowedRoles. No behaviour change. This is the seam tests/helpers/routeWalker.js reads to produce route-inventory.json; it also revealed that 15 routers apply guards via a pathless router.use() rather than per-route, and that studentRoutes.js does both (an intersection no grep would have shown).

title: A non-fresh test database surfaced as dozens of unrelated assertion failures instead of one clear error
repro: Suites build fixtures with fixed natural keys (batch abbreviation 'TB', known emails). If the DROP/CREATE does not take effect, the first fixture insert 400s, the suite's beforeAll throws, and every case in that file fails. Observed once in Phase 2 (see B-006).
fix: Assert immediately after seeding that "users" holds exactly the one seeded admin, and fail with an explanatory message naming the likely cause. Converts a 32-failure cascade into a single diagnosable error.

title: authMiddleware allowlist uses startsWith, so it exempts path prefixes rather than paths
repro: Two of the five allowlist checks are prefix matches: req.path.startsWith('/api-docs') and req.path.startsWith('/api/samples'). GET /api/samplesXYZ, /api/samples-secret and /api-docsFOO all skip authentication entirely and return 404 (proven in tests/int/authz-matrix.test.js), whereas an unmatched path that is NOT on the allowlist correctly returns 401. No route currently lives under those prefixes, so this is a latent footgun rather than a live data leak — but any future route matching the prefix is silently unauthenticated.
recommendation: Replace the prefix tests with exact matches plus an explicit '/api-docs/' and '/api/samples/' boundary check, e.g. p === '/api-docs' || p.startsWith('/api-docs/'). Characterisation tests pin the current behaviour, so they will fail loudly and must be updated when the fix lands.

title: Any authenticated principal can read every notification and mark any notification read
repro: notificationRoutes.js applies no authorizeRoles. GET /api/notifications and PUT /api/notifications/:id/read are reachable by ADMIN, TEACHER and STUDENT alike (confirmed by the authorization matrix). Notification ids are sequential integers, so a STUDENT can enumerate and mark read any other user's notifications. POST /api/notifications is protected, but by a hand-rolled local ensureAdmin (lines 8-13) rather than authorizeRoles, so the guard is invisible to the route inventory and is tracked as KNOWN_UNTAGGED_GUARDS.
recommendation: Scope both read paths to the calling user (req.user.id) inside the controller, and replace the local ensureAdmin with authorizeRoles('ADMIN') so the policy is introspectable. Also drop the unused authMiddleware import at line 3.

title: All three schedule routes are open to any authenticated principal
repro: scheduleRoutes.js declares no authorizeRoles on GET /api/schedule/today, /week or /full; the matrix confirms all three are reachable by every role. A STUDENT can read the full institutional timetable, not just their own. Also imports authMiddleware at line 3 and never uses it.
recommendation: Decide the intended audience per route and add authorizeRoles accordingly; if STUDENT access is intended, scope the response to the caller's section rather than returning the full schedule.

title: Observed once and not reproduced: all 32 teacher-portal cases failed while the other three suites passed
repro: During one Phase 2 run of `npm test`, 32 failed / 45 passed — the 45 being authz-matrix (28) + credential-delivery (14) + associations (3), i.e. the entire teacher-portal file went down together, the signature of its beforeAll throwing. Coverage for that run was correspondingly lower (640 branch total vs 867). Did not reproduce in 8 subsequent runs, including the exact back-to-back command sequence that preceded it.
recommendation: Most likely cause is cross-run interference: forceExit is false and loggingMiddleware fires an unawaited AuditLog.create after each response (B-001), so a previous Jest process can still be doing work while globalSetup drops and recreates the database. A-013 adds a freshness tripwire so a recurrence fails with a named cause instead of a cascade. Revisit when Phase 4 introduces truncate-between-suites isolation.

title: /uploads is served by express.static before authMiddleware — existing files are world-readable
repro: app.use('/uploads', express.static(...)) sits ~20 lines above app.use(authMiddleware). Confirmed behaviourally: an anonymous GET for a file that exists returns 200 with its contents, while a GET for a nonexistent file falls through to auth and returns 401. Only real files are exposed — which is why a missing-file probe would have looked fine and proven nothing. Uploaded avatars are readable by anyone who can guess or enumerate a filename.
recommendation: Serve uploads through an authenticated route that streams from disk, or issue short-lived signed URLs. Not a drop-in fix: moving the mount below authMiddleware breaks every in both the Angular admin and the Flutter client, so the clients must be updated in the same change. Characterisation tests in authz-matrix.test.js pin the current exposure.
